- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly above true outcome, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is below true outcome, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0, model tends to overestimate; apply a 3–5% downward correction to the next 3–5 days.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), forecast should not overshoot upward; cap upward moves at 2–3% above recent high.  
- If forecast shows sharp upward spike followed by true outcome reversal, reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for next 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 2–3% below forecast, apply a 2–3% downward bias correction for next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend but price is trending upward, forecast should not lag by more than 1–2 days; adjust to align with recent 5-day moving average.
